newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIAN BOWLERS TIGHTEN GRIP ON AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIAN BOWLERS TIGHTEN GRIP ON AUSTRALIA.

text.p: India's bowlers tightened their grip on the one-off test when they removed four front-ranking batsmen to leave Australia struggling at 79 for four in their second innings at tea on Saturday.
Australia were bundled out for 182 on the opening day and fell 179 runs behind after India amassed 361 in their first innings.

Ricky Ponting, who had survived a confident caught-behind appeal after Michael Slater was dismissed for nought by debutant medium-pacer David Johnson, was bowled by an in-cutter from Venkatesh Prasad for 13.
Captain Mark Taylor, batting with confidence, and Mark Waugh repaired the damage to add 47 runs for the third wicket.

Taylor steered and square cut left-arm spinner Sunil Joshi to the fence in quick succession. Mark Waugh then cut Joshi for two boundaries as the Australian batsmen came to terms with the Indian attack.
But Mark Waugh was adjudged caught behind off leg-spinner Anil Kumble as he shaped for a square-cut. He was not satisfied with the verdict of English umpire Peter Willey.
Mark Waugh's 23 runs came in 80 minutes off 66 balls and included four boundaries.
Six runs later Taylor also perished. He plodded forward against off-spinner Aashish Kapoor and popped up a simple bat-pad catch to Vikram Rathore at forward short-leg.
Taylor struck four boundaries from the 112 balls faced in his patient, 149-minute 37.
